# Capricorn

A private, encrypted screen and clipboard history for Hyprland on NixOS. Find that command, snippet or message you saw last week, without handing your screen to anyone else.

## Installation

Capricorn ships as a Nix flake with a NixOS module (the vault daemon) and a Home Manager
module (screen capture, the search overlay and Hyprland integration). It needs Hyprland
0.49 or newer for the screencopy permission system.

```nix
# flake.nix
{
  inputs.capricorn.url = "github:Garulf/capricorn";

  outputs = { nixpkgs, home-manager, capricorn, ... }: {
    nixosConfigurations.laptop = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
      modules = [
        capricorn.nixosModules.default
        {
          services.capricorn = {
            enable = true;
            users = [ "alice" ];      # each user needs an explicit uid
          };
        }
        home-manager.nixosModules.home-manager
        {
          home-manager.users.alice = {
            imports = [ capricorn.homeManagerModules.default ];
            programs.capricorn.enable = true;
          };
        }
      ];
    };
  };
}
```

The NixOS module refuses to build on a host where captured data could reach disk in the
clear: unencrypted swap, hibernation to an unencrypted device, or stored core dumps. See
[docs/security.md](docs/security.md) for why, and `services.capricorn.allowInsecureHost`
if you really need to override it.

## Usage

Create the vault once. The password is separate from your login password, and the
recovery code is the only way back in if you forget it, so write it down and keep it
offline.

```sh
capricorn init
```

Recording starts as soon as the capture service runs. It keeps going while the vault is
locked: new captures are encrypted with the vault's public key and become searchable the
next time you unlock.

### Keybinds

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `SUPER + ALT + R` | Search overlay |
| `SUPER + ALT + T` | Timeline |
| `SUPER + ALT + L` | Lock the vault |
| `SUPER + ALT + P` | Pause or resume recording |

Change them with `programs.capricorn.keybinds.*`, or set one to `null` to drop it. The
Home Manager module writes Lua when `wayland.windowManager.hyprland.configType = "lua"`
and hyprlang otherwise.

In the search overlay, Enter opens the moment in the timeline, Ctrl+C copies the matched
text, Ctrl+O reopens the app on its old workspace (terminals in the same directory,
browsers on the same page when it was captured) and Esc closes it.

### Command line

```sh
capricorn status              # vault and recorder state
capricorn search nix flake    # asks for the password, prints matches
capricorn search --json --kind clipboard token
capricorn forget 10           # drop the last 10 minutes
capricorn pause / resume
capricorn lock
capricorn passwd
```

### Locking

The vault locks after 15 minutes without use (`services.capricorn.lockTimeout`), on
suspend, and when logind locks your session. If you lock with hyprlock through hypridle,
add Capricorn to the lock command:

```nix
services.hypridle.settings.general.lock_cmd = "capricorn lock; pidof hyprlock || hyprlock";
```

### Waybar

```json
"custom/capricorn": {
  "exec": "capricorn status --waybar --follow",
  "return-type": "json",
  "on-click": "capricorn show search"
}
```

The module's `class` is one of `recording`, `paused`, `idle`, `locked` or `off`.

### Keeping things out

Password managers (KeePassXC, Bitwarden, 1Password and others) and private browser
windows are never recorded. Add your own rules:

```nix
programs.capricorn.exclude = [
  { class = "^signal$"; }
  { title = "bank"; }
  { workspace = "9"; }
];
```

Clipboard entries marked as secret by password managers, and anything that looks like an
API token, key or JWT, are never stored. The same patterns are blurred out of screenshots
before they are saved.

### Retention

History is kept for 90 days or 50 GiB, whichever comes first. Both are configurable,
including `null` for forever:

```nix
services.capricorn.retention = {
  days = null;
  maxGiB = 200;
  clipboardDays = 7;
};
```

## How it stays private

- Nothing leaves the machine. The daemon runs as its own system user with no network
  access.
- History is encrypted at rest and readable only after you unlock with your password.
  Programs running as you can't read the files, even while you are using your desktop.
- Recording only needs the vault's public key, so whatever records can't read back what
  it recorded.

The full threat model, including what this does not protect against, is in
[docs/security.md](docs/security.md).

## Limitations

- Hyprland only, Wayland only.
- Password manager popups inside a browser window can't be excluded by window rules.
- While the vault is unlocked and on screen, anything that can see your screen can see
  your history.
